title: Podman exec build wrong enviroment
body:
### Issue Description

I created a podman precreate hook to set some env vairbales. With `podman exec` I can not see them.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create a OCI hook
``` 
cat  /usr/share/containers/oci/hooks.d/test.json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "hook": {
    "path": "/example.sh"
  },
  "when": {
    "always": true
  },
  "stages": [
    "precreate"
  ]
}
```
with 
``` 
cat /example.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

config=$(cat)


jq '.process.env += ["FOO=BAR"]' <<<"$config"
``` 

2. Create a container and check the env.
` podman run --rm  --name test   alpine  env` will give you `FOO=BAR`
but with `podman run --rm  --name test  -d alpine sleep infinity` and `podman exec test env`  this env is missing.





### Describe the results you received

The resulting config seems to be correct, it is in 
1.  `podman inspect test  | jq '.[0].Config.Env'`
2. also PID 1 has the env variable `podman exec test cat  /proc/1/environ  | tr "\0" "\n" `

It seems like the parent process ID of a exec is 0 and not 1 therefore my guess is, that the exec misses some env variable source

### Describe the results you expected

If a set a env via a hook, i also want to see them with `podman exec`

comments.body:
I'd like to work on this.

I've traced the root cause: podman exec builds its process spec from the container's stored config (set before hooks run), while the running container launches from the post-hook spec that podman writes to the bundle config.json. podman inspect and exec capability handling already read that on-disk spec, so exec is the odd one out.

I have a fix that makes exec read the on-disk spec (falling back to the stored config when it does not exist) plus a bats regression test. PR coming shortly.
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.
